memory_update.text: For enterprise AI software/data/automation, primary US-listed coverage should include MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, ORCL, CRM, NOW, PLTR, SNOW, DDOG, MDB, ESTC, CFLT, PATH, CRWD, and ADBE.

The node is not a single vertical; it spans cloud AI platforms, systems of record, data readiness, workflow automation, observability, cybersecurity, and application-layer monetization. Claims should be separated between direct AI software revenue and second-order infrastructure enablement.

Important adjacent US-listed names not included due to the 15-candidate cap but worth future checks: IBM, Accenture, Workday, Atlassian, Intuit, HubSpot, Monday.com, Appian, Pegasystems, Box, Dropbox, Okta, Zscaler, Palo Alto Networks, and Cloudflare.

AI revenue disclosure remains inconsistent across the universe. The next layer should penalize companies where AI language is not tied to paid usage, ARR/product revenue, consumption, backlog, customer wins, renewal rates, or margin evidence.

Falsification plan: downgrade the node if enterprise AI pilots fail to convert to production deployments, if cloud AI consumption growth slows despite product launches, if net retention weakens, if AI features cause margin dilution without pricing power, or if customers cite data governance/security/change-management barriers as delaying adoption.

node: Enterprise AI software, data platforms, workflow automation, and application-layer deployment
summary: Expanded US-listed universe for the enterprise AI software/data/automation deployment node. The screen emphasizes companies that may determine whether AI infrastructure demand becomes durable: cloud AI platforms, enterprise copilots/agents, data readiness layers, workflow automation, observability, security, and integration. Inclusion is for research coverage only, not a buy/sell view. Most relations are inference-level because direct AI revenue disclosure remains uneven across the group; next work should verify AI-specific revenue, consumption growth, attach rates, customer deployments, net retention, regulated-industry adoption, and gross-margin effects.
